The fix is in: `split_cents(100, 3)` now returns `[33, 33, 34]`. When a total doesn't divide evenly, the leftover grosze go one each to the last people in the list, so the shares always add up to the total.

I also had to change one other file. `receipt.py` was working around the old bug by adding the whole remainder to the last person's share. With the fix in place, that line would have added the leftover grosze twice, so I removed it. Receipts look the same as before when one grosz is left over (3,33 / 3,33 / 3,34 zł). When more is left over, it's now spread across people: 10,01 zł split three ways gives 3,33 / 3,34 / 3,34 instead of 3,33 / 3,33 / 3,35.

I added a test for uneven splits to `test_money.py`. Because I changed `receipt.py`, I also ran `test_receipt.py` along with `test_money.py`. It's small and quick, and all 6 tests pass. I skipped the full suite as you asked, and I haven't committed anything.
